headline: Gemini Notebook switches to compute-based usage limits starting Sept 2, 2026
summary: Google's Gemini Notebook will adopt compute-based usage limits, similar to other Gemini products, replacing its simpler prompt-based system. Quotas will now refresh every 5 hours instead of daily.
details: Google is changing Gemini Notebook's usage limits to a compute-based model, effective September 2, 2026. This aligns it with how the main Gemini product already calculates usage, factoring in prompt complexity, context, and features used.

Previously, Gemini Notebook (then NotebookLM) used simple daily prompt-based limits, unlike ChatGPT and Claude which used token consumption. The main Gemini product switched to a compute-used model with a five-hour refresh window after I/O 2026.

The new system means limits are based on the complexity of prompts, models/features used, and chat length. If limits are hit, users can return after 5 hours when the quota refreshes, or upgrade their plan for higher limits.
Free plan users get "standard limits." AI Plus offers 2x, Pro 4x, and AI Ultra plans provide 5x or 20x higher usage depending on the $100 or $200 tier.
The notebook will suggest alternative outputs if a choice surpasses limits. Users can also schedule Video Overviews or Slide Decks to be generated later, receiving a notification upon completion.

headline_marked: [[TurboKV: Insanely fast Rust key-value store]] with atomic batches and hardware AES
headline: TurboKV: Insanely fast Rust key-value store with atomic batches and hardware AES
summary: TurboKV is an async embedded key-value database for Rust, featuring atomic batches, ordered range scans, configurable durability, compression, and background compaction.
details: TurboKV is an async embedded key-value database built in Rust, designed for high performance. It supports atomic batches, ordered range scans, configurable durability, compression, and background compaction.

The database utilizes a persisted Bloom-filter format that leverages hardware AES for enhanced speed. Developers can optimize builds for x86/x86_64 targets with RUSTFLAGS="-C target-feature=+aes,+sse2" and for ARM/AArch64 with "-C target-feature=+aes,+neon".

Each database instance or engine exclusively owns its data directory. Keys and values are arbitrary byte sequences, with mutation APIs copying inputs before returning and point reads providing owned Vec<u8> values.
All presets for TurboKV start with a 64 MiB memtable, a 64 MiB block cache, and LZ4 compression. These public fields can be adjusted before opening the database, allowing for tailored performance.

With the Write-Ahead Log (WAL) enabled, each record or complete batch must fit within the WAL's u32 payload length. The `DbOptions::durable()` preset offers process-crash recovery, while `DbOptions::paranoid()` ensures sync-before-acknowledgement durability.
Keys are ordered lexicographically by raw bytes, and every scan captures a coherent point-in-time view. Frequent small scans can freeze active memtables, potentially increasing later flush work.

Benchmarking on an Apple M4 chip showed TurboKV 0.6.0 compared against fjall 2.11.2 and redb 2.6.3. The tests used 200,000 deterministic 20-byte keys and 400-byte values, with compression and block cache disabled.
caption:
Meet TurboKV: an insanely fast, async embedded key-value store written in Rust.

TurboKV is an async embedded key-value database built in Rust, designed for high performance. It supports atomic batches, ordered range scans, configurable durability, compression, and background compaction.

The database utilizes a persisted Bloom-filter format that leverages hardware AES for enhanced speed. Developers can optimize builds for x86/x86_64 targets with RUSTFLAGS="-C target-feature=+aes,+sse2" and for ARM/AArch64 with "-C target-feature=+aes,+neon".

Each database instance or engine exclusively owns its data directory. Keys and values are arbitrary byte sequences, with mutation APIs copying inputs before returning and point reads providing owned Vec<u8> values.

All presets for TurboKV start with a 64 MiB memtable, a 64 MiB block cache, and LZ4 compression. These public fields can be adjusted before opening the database, allowing for tailored performance.

With the Write-Ahead Log (WAL) enabled, each record or complete batch must fit within the WAL's u32 payload length. The `DbOptions::durable()` preset offers process-crash recovery, while `DbOptions::paranoid()` ensures sync-before-acknowledgement durability.

Keys are ordered lexicographically by raw bytes, and every scan captures a coherent point-in-time view. Frequent small scans can freeze active memtables, potentially increasing later flush work.

Benchmarking on an Apple M4 chip showed TurboKV 0.6.0 compared against fjall 2.11.2 and redb 2.6.3. The tests used 200,000 deterministic 20-byte keys and 400-byte values, with compression and block cache disabled.
